title: Throughput
hook: Working longer hours isn't the same as getting more done. Usually it's one extra step slowing everything down.
statement: How fast you produce output matters more than how much effort you put in.
explainer: Effort feels like progress, but throughput is what clients and revenue actually see. Cutting one useless step often beats trying to go faster at everything.
sop: Time one full cycle of work, start to finish.
Work out your Throughput: Output ÷ Time.
Cut or combine steps that don't add value.
Batch similar tasks instead of bouncing between them.
Re-time the cycle to confirm it actually got faster.
equation_example: You finished 12 client projects, your Output, in 30 days, your Time. 12 ÷ 30 = 0.4 projects a day. Higher means you're producing faster without working longer. Falling with the same hours means something is slowing you down.
question: Pick one process and name the step you could remove to double your throughput.
closing_statement: Removing a step beats rushing through it.
caption:
Principle Nº 119: Throughput

Working longer hours isn't the same as getting more done. Usually it's one extra step slowing everything down.

How fast you produce output matters more than how much effort you put in.

Your turn: Pick one process and name the step you could remove to double your throughput.
